details.title: Arban – Ornament Study No. 77
details.lead: From Arban's Grande méthode complète de cornet à pistons et de saxhorn, first edition, 1864. The notes are the cornet part as printed, in written pitch for the B♭ cornet. Below: the book's own words, translated from the French.
facts: Arban, Grande méthode complète de cornet à pistons et de saxhorn, first edition (Paris: Léon Escudier, 1864)

Most trills begin with three small notes and close with two. After the slowing in bars 30 and 31 the first part comes back at the first speed, and ends in F. In bars 5, 21, 37 and 47 the book prints the valves under the small notes before the trill: F sharp with 1 2 3, G with 1 3, A with 3. They hold for the whole trill, so that it stays in one series of the horn and the lips do the work.

sections.heading: The trill
paragraphs: On valve instruments the trill is the hardest of all the ornaments. Only the half-step trill is really bearable. Whole-step trills can be made, but take care to press the valves down evenly, so that each beat is quite distinct.

So first work patiently, and without hurrying, at studies Nos. 60 to 67, until each sound comes out cleanly. Later you can play the studies on the trill, following the fingerings shown exactly. (See Nos. 68 to 80.)

sections.heading: A word on all of these
paragraphs: Since all the lessons on ornaments were written to serve as studies, I have brought together, on purpose and in abundance, every kind of ornament. But take great care not to overuse them so in practice, for that would be in the worst of taste.

sources.title: IMSLP: Grande méthode complète de cornet à pistons (Arban), first edition, Paris 1864
